S72.01.needs: a signed-in AGI account (agi login) or a saved provider key
S72.01.note: The launch path with no arguments was not traced step by step; the start hint text is built from the keybinding for the command palette.
steps: Open Terminal, go to any project folder and type agi, then press Enter.
Look for a full-screen screen with a composer at the bottom and the start hint line that says "for commands".
Type a short question such as "say hello" and press Enter.
Look for your message and an answer in the transcript above the composer, and compare with Expected.
S72.01.where: Type agi in a terminal with no arguments, then the start screen line "Type / for commands"

labels.text: Whether this run renders in plain mode

S72.02.needs: a signed-in AGI account or a provider key
S72.02.note: The code also has a screen-reader mode switched on by the AGI_SCREEN_READER environment variable that adds a label; it is not a visible control, and the exact plain-mode behaviour was not run.
steps: In Terminal, type agi --plain exec "say hello in one line" and press Enter.
Look for plain text only: no colour, no spinner, no horizontal rules and no full-screen redraw.
Compare the lines printed with the ones that appear one after another in order.
S72.02.where: agi --plain exec "<your question>" in a terminal (--plain is the flag; AGI_SCREEN_READER is an environment variable with no screen control)

S72.03.needs: a signed-in AGI account or a provider key
steps: In Terminal, type agi exec "say hello in one word" and press Enter.
Look for the answer printed and the shell prompt returning on its own, with no full-screen UI.
Type echo $? and press Enter; expect 0 after a successful run.
S72.03.where: agi exec "<your prompt>" in a terminal (alias agi e)

labels.text: Read prompt from stdin (auto-detected when stdin is piped)

S72.04.needs: a signed-in AGI account or a provider key
steps: In Terminal, type echo "say hello in one word" | agi --stdin and press Enter.
Look for the answer printed and the shell prompt returning.
Compare with Expected: the prompt text came from stdin, not from the command line.
S72.04.where: echo "<your prompt>" | agi --stdin in a terminal, or echo "<your prompt>" | agi -

labels.text: Read prompt from stdin (auto-detected when stdin is piped)

S72.05.needs: a git project with an uncommitted change, and a signed-in AGI account
S72.05.note: The auto-detection of piped stdin is in the top-level code path; the --file flag was not run.
steps: Make a small change to a tracked file in a git project.
In Terminal, type git diff | agi "explain this diff" and press Enter.
Look for an answer that talks about the change you made, and that the prompt text and the diff were both used.
Optionally run agi -f <a file> "summarize" and check the answer uses that file.
S72.05.where: git diff | agi "explain this diff" in a git folder with an uncommitted change

labels.text: Print output without any formatting (raw text only)

S72.06.needs: a signed-in AGI account or a provider key
steps: In Terminal, type agi --raw "say hello in one word" and press Enter.
Look for only the answer text: no spinner, no cost line and no formatting.
Compare with Expected.
S72.06.where: agi --raw "<your prompt>" in a terminal (also agi --print or agi --output-format text)

labels.text: Output format for the one-shot response and for

S72.07.needs: a signed-in AGI account or a provider key
S72.07.note: The exact JSON field names were not read in this pass.
steps: In Terminal, type agi exec --json "say hello in one word" and press Enter.
Look for one JSON object printed on its own.
Check the object has the answer and fields for tokens, cost, duration and error state, and compare with Expected.
S72.07.where: agi exec --json "<your prompt>" in a terminal (or agi --output-format json "<your prompt>")

labels.text: Newline-delimited JSON for streaming consumption (CI/CD compatible)

S72.08.needs: a signed-in AGI account or a provider key
S72.08.note: The value name stream-json is inferred from the enum variant StreamJson; the exact event names were not read.
steps: In Terminal, type agi --output-format stream-json "say hello in one word" and press Enter.
Look for one JSON event per line appearing while the answer is being produced.
Compare the events with Expected: session start, user message, text, tool events, final message and end or error.
S72.08.where: agi --output-format stream-json "<your prompt>" in a terminal

S72.09.needs: a signed-out state (agi logout) and a terminal
S72.09.note: The mapping is in the code (exit code per error class); the exact code for each situation was not run.
steps: Run agi exec "hello" while signed out and with no provider key.
Type echo $? and press Enter.
Compare the number with Expected: 77 for not permitted, or 78 for a configuration problem.
S72.09.where: Exit status of agi in a terminal, shown with echo $?

labels.text: Sign in to your AGI account, or store a provider API key.

S72.10.needs: an AGI account; the browser sign-in step needs a web browser
steps: In Terminal, type agi auth-status and press Enter; note the account line.
Type agi login and follow the browser sign-in prompt, then run agi auth-status again.
Type agi logout and press Enter, then agi auth-status; expect a signed-out line.
Compare with Expected.
S72.10.where: agi login, agi logout, agi auth-status in a terminal; /login, /logout and /status in the TUI

S72.11.needs: at least one earlier session on this device
S72.11.note: The agi session list subcommand was not separately checked.
steps: Run one prompt in agi so a session exists, then exit with Ctrl+D twice.
Start agi again and type /history, then press Enter.
Look for the picker titled Sessions listing saved sessions; use the arrow keys to move and press Esc to close.
In a second Terminal window, type agi history and press Enter; compare the list with the picker.
S72.11.where: /history in the TUI (picker titled Sessions); agi history in a terminal

labels.text: Continue the newest session started in this project

steps: Start agi and type /resume, then press Enter.
In the Sessions picker, use the arrow keys to choose a session and press Enter.
Look for a notice that says Resumed session with the message count, and the earlier messages in the transcript.
Compare with Expected.
S72.12.where: /resume in the TUI; agi resume in a terminal; agi -c for the newest session in this folder

S72.13.needs: an existing conversation with at least one message
S72.13.note: The exact notice text after a fork was not read.
steps: In a session with at least one exchange, type /fork and press Enter.
Look for a new session created from this one, with the earlier messages copied in.
Type /history and press Enter to see both sessions listed.
S72.13.where: /fork or /branch in the TUI; agi fork <session id> in a terminal

S72.14.needs: a signed-in AGI account with more than one model available
S72.14.note: The picker title was not found in this pass.
steps: Start agi and type /model, then press Enter.
Use the arrow keys to choose another model and press Enter.
Look for the banner Model changed to followed by the model name.
Send a short prompt and compare with Expected.
S72.14.where: /model in the TUI (opens the model picker); /model <id> to set it directly

S72.15.note: That the next request actually uses the new level cannot be seen on screen from the code path alone.
steps: Start agi and type /effort, then press Enter.
Look for the picker titled Effort; use the arrow keys or Tab to choose low, medium, high or max, then press Enter.
Look for the notice Effort set to followed by the chosen level.
Send a short prompt and compare with Expected.
S72.15.where: /effort in the TUI (opens the picker titled Effort); /effort low, /effort med, /effort high from the composer

steps: Start agi and type /permissions, then press Enter.
Look for the line Permissions: followed by Recently denied, Allow, Ask, Deny and Workspace.
Press Shift+Tab and watch the mode change.
Compare with Expected.
S72.16.where: /permissions in the TUI (aliases /perms, /approvals); Shift+Tab to cycle the permission mode

S72.17.note: The report wording was not read.
steps: In a conversation with several messages, type /context and press Enter.
Look for a report of how full the context window is.
If the conversation is near full, look for the notice Context is N% full.
Compare with Expected.
Start agi and type /usage, then press Enter.
Look for the panel titled Usage showing session tokens and cost and the account allowance.
Press Esc to close the panel (it says Esc to close).
Compare with Expected.
S72.18.where: /usage in the TUI (opens the Usage panel)

labels.text: /compact summarizes earlier turns to make room

S72.19.note: The before and after size report wording was not read.
steps: In a long conversation, type /compact and press Enter; or type /compact keep the database decisions and press Enter.
Look for the summary step finish and a report of the size before and after.
Compare with Expected.

labels.text: Manage the global MCP server registry

S72.20.needs: an MCP server to add, or none to list
S72.20.note: The authenticate and remove subcommand names were not confirmed in this pass.
steps: In a terminal, type agi mcp list and press Enter; note the servers shown.
Type /mcp in the TUI and press Enter; look for the connected servers and tools.
Compare with Expected. Add, inspect, authenticate and remove were not run.
S72.20.where: agi mcp list and agi mcp add <name> in a terminal; /mcp in the TUI

S72.21.needs: none to list; a plugin to install or update
S72.21.note: Install and update were not traced; the skills toggle screen was not read in full.
steps: Start agi and type /skills, then press Enter; look for the skills list with on and off toggles.
Type /plugins and press Enter; look for the plugins list.
In a terminal type agi plugin and press Enter; compare the list with the TUI.
S72.21.where: /skills and /plugins in the TUI; agi plugin in a terminal

S72.22.note: The /add-dir command is dispatched only in the parity REPL file, not in the TUI command list, so it was not confirmed in the TUI.
steps: In a terminal, type agi -C ~/some/other/folder and press Enter, then ask what folder it is in.
Type agi --add-dir <another folder> "list the files in it" and press Enter.
Compare the answer with the folder named.
S72.22.where: agi -C <folder> "<prompt>" in a terminal; agi --add-dir <folder> "<prompt>"; /add-dir <folder> in the REPL

steps: Start agi in a project folder.
Type @ at the start of a word and look for the popup headed Files.
Type part of a file name to filter it, press Enter to pick it, then send a question about the file.
Check the answer uses the content of the chosen file.
S72.23.where: Type @ in the composer of the TUI (opens the Files popup)

S72.24.note: The key for reverse history search was not confirmed in this pass.
steps: Start agi, type a prompt such as hello one and press Enter, then exit with Ctrl+D twice.
Start agi again and press the Up arrow in the empty composer.
Look for hello one appearing in the composer.
Compare with Expected.
S72.24.where: Up and Down arrows in the TUI composer; history persists across runs

S72.25.needs: none; a config file to rebind
S72.25.note: The rebinding itself was not run; the config path is from the config code.
steps: Start agi and type /keys, then press Enter.
Look for the heading Keybindings and the list of actions with their keys.
Compare with the bindings in ~/.agiworkforce/config.toml under [ui.keybindings] (rebinding is done there).
Compare with Expected.
S72.25.where: /keys or /keybindings in the TUI; config in the file ~/.agiworkforce/config.toml under [ui.keybindings]

S72.26.note: The older flag `--completions <SHELL>` still works as a deprecated alias (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:288) and `completions` is also accepted as the command name.
steps: Open a terminal and type `agi completion bash`, then press Enter.
Look for a printed bash completion script for the agi command (a function and a complete line for agi).
Repeat with `agi completion zsh` and `agi completion fish`.
Compare: each shell prints its own script with no error, as Expected says.
S72.26.where: Terminal: agi completion bash (also zsh or fish)

S72.27.note: The choice is saved to the project settings file (save_project_ui_settings in apps/cli/src/config.rs), not a global file, and `/theme <slug>` sets it directly. Esc closes the picker without a change.
steps: Type `agi` and press Enter to open the full-screen app.
Type `/theme` and press Enter to open the theme picker.
Press Down or j to move to another row (for example High Contrast Dark), then press Enter.
Look for the message `Theme set to <name>, saved in <path>.` and for the screen colours changing. Quit and run `agi` again to check the theme is kept. Compare with Expected.
S72.27.where: Terminal: agi, then type /theme and press Enter

labels.text: Plain output for a screen reader

S72.28.note: --plain switches to the line-based screen reader mode instead of the full-screen app. NO_COLOR is checked in apps/cli/src/output.rs (detect_color_level) and in apps/cli/src/tui/icons.rs, but I did not find a check of NO_COLOR for the full-screen app's colours, so that part is unsure.
steps: Type `agi --plain` and press Enter.
Type a short question and look for plain text with no coloured words, no spinner and no box rules.
Optionally type `NO_COLOR=1 agi` and press Enter, then check the colours in the full-screen app.

S72.29.note: Resizing is handled by the terminal redraw; no control exists. The matching regression test name is in apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs but is not a visible word, so it is not used as a label.
steps: Type `agi` and press Enter, then send one short question so the transcript has text.
Drag a corner of the terminal window to make it narrower, then wider.
Look for the transcript still showing the same messages, with the text re-wrapped to the new width. Compare with Expected.
S72.29.where: Terminal window resize while agi's full-screen app is open

labels.text: Bring a cloud Code session here
Continue previous session, from this device or from your account.

S72.30.needs: a cloud Code session on your AGI account whose repository is on GitHub; for --teleport, a local checkout of that repository
S72.30.note: Teleport fails with a message for sessions with no GitHub repository or no working branch yet.
steps: In a checkout of the GitHub repository a cloud session used, type `agi resume --teleport` and press Enter, then pick a session.
Or type `agi resume <id> --cloud` with an id from your account.
Look for the message `Checked out` or `Updated` with the branch name and remote, then the session history shown in the app.
Compare with Expected: the session continues from its cloud history.
S72.30.where: Terminal: agi resume --teleport (picker), agi resume --teleport <id>, or agi resume <id> --cloud

S72.31.needs: none for background runs; for /tasks stop, a task that is running in the session (for example a sub-agent)
S72.31.note: Expected mentions long-running commands; the code only shows prompt runs and sub-agent tasks. The /tasks stop subcommand is in apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs.
steps: Type `agi background start "<a short prompt>"` and press Enter to start a background run.
Type `agi background list` and press Enter; find the run id.
Type `agi background logs <id>` to see its output, then `agi background stop <id>` to stop it.
In the app, type `/tasks` and press Enter to list this session's tasks; compare the list and stop state with Expected.
S72.31.where: Terminal: agi background list (also logs <id>, stop <id>); in the app: type /tasks and press Enter

labels.text: already exists, so nothing was written

S72.32.needs: a conversation with at least one message
S72.32.note: Export writes to a file or the screen only; I did not find a clipboard export in the export code, so the clipboard part of Expected is unsure. The JSON form is `/export json <file>`.
steps: Have a conversation with at least one message.
Type `/export` and press Enter; look for the Markdown transcript shown on screen.
Type `/export transcript.md` and press Enter; look for `Exported the conversation to <path>.`
Type the same command again; look for the refusal that the file already exists. Compare with Expected.
S72.32.where: In the app: type /export and press Enter, or /export <file name> and press Enter

S72.33.needs: a project config file in .agiworkforce/ (optional, for the override check)
S72.33.note: The global file is resolved by the config root (apps/cli/src/config.rs:15 and :491).
steps: In a project folder that has a .agiworkforce/config.toml file, type `agi --config` and press Enter.
Look for the `Sources:` section with the global path and the project path.
Compare the values shown with the config.toml files on disk.
Type `/config` in the app and compare the same values.
S72.33.where: Terminal: agi --config, or in the app: /config

S72.34.needs: none; a model id you can use for the model check
S72.34.note: The env override list is built in apps/cli/src/config.rs around line 1665; the env var names are listed in apps/cli/src/config.rs around line 1634.
steps: Type `agi --config` with no extra variables and press Enter; note the `Env:` line says none.
Type `AGI_PLAIN=1 agi --config` and press Enter; look for AGI_PLAIN listed on the `Env:` line.
Type `AGIWORKFORCE_MODEL=<a model id from /model> agi --config` and press Enter; look for the model value and AGIWORKFORCE_MODEL on the `Env:` line.
Compare with Expected: the override is shown.
S72.34.where: Terminal: AGIWORKFORCE_MODEL=<model id> agi --config (or AGI_PLAIN=1 agi --config)

labels.text: Compare this build against the newest published CLI release.
No signed AGI CLI release is published yet.

S72.35.needs: none; the install step does not finish until the owner publishes a signed release
S72.35.note: Expected cannot be met yet: the code notes the release signing key is not set (the owner task in the plan). The install command is from apps/cli/README.md line 29.
steps: Run `curl -fsSL https://agiworkforce.com/install.sh | bash` in a terminal and press Enter.
Read the installer output: it currently stops with a message that no signed release is published.
Run `agi update --check` and press Enter.
Look for the comparison of the running version with the newest published release, as Expected says.
S72.35.where: Terminal: curl -fsSL https://agiworkforce.com/install.sh | bash, then agi update --check

steps: Type `agi doctor` and press Enter.
Read the list of checks and their status words.
Type `agi doctor --json` and press Enter; look for one JSON report.
Type `agi doctor --export` and press Enter; note the file it says it wrote and check it is marked as redacted. Compare with Expected.
S72.36.where: Terminal: agi doctor (also agi doctor --json, agi doctor --export)

labels.text: Stop the session when total spend exceeds this many USD.
Auto-approve safe tool calls (reads, searches, listings).

S72.37.needs: a signed-in account that can run a prompt
S72.37.note: I did not confirm that --max-budget-usd and --mode are accepted after the exec subcommand; check `agi exec --help`. Exit code values are covered by S72.09.
steps: Type `agi exec --output-format json "say hello"` and press Enter; look for one JSON result on the screen with no spinner.
Type `agi exec --json-events --max-budget-usd 0.01 "<a longer task>"` and press Enter; look for NDJSON events and a status_update with reason budget_exhausted.
Type `echo $?` and press Enter; look for a non-zero exit code when the run stops.
Use `--mode` to set the permission policy and check the run does not ask for input. Compare with Expected.
S72.37.where: Terminal: agi exec with --output-format json, --json-events, --max-budget-usd and --mode
